industry.why: Underweight, from Neutral, on the special topic 'Why the Defence Industry de-rated from July to October 2026 while Theon's forecasts rose' and on the condition written on this row last week, which fired: a third reading at F with no demand read in the strategist sources. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): the Researcher's report finds multiples cut while estimates held, the industry's premium over the STOXX 600 down from 60% to 12% (Bernstein, 9-Oct-26), exit multiples moving towards 13 times operating profit as the order boom gives way to execution (Jefferies, 28-Oct-26, 'Defense Likely at Peak Fundamentals vs. Aero'), and budgets converting slowly into contracts (German run-rate, Boxer approvals); the UK Budget funded the existing Defence Investment Plan but postponed the 3%-of-output decision to the 2027 Spending Review. One live holding, Theon (4.05%), judged in components 4 and 5; no Pool name sits here, so the Lists are unmoved. Counter-case: estimates have not fallen, the premium compression may already be the exit multiple, and German approvals may convert (Rheinmetall 5-Nov-26, Bundestag budget vote 27-Nov-26). Back to C if relative strength leaves F as approvals convert; to F on a signed Ukraine settlement followed by defence fund outflows.

memo.verdict: Neutral at 30.96 EUR (2026-09-24); bullish at or below 30 EUR, the price at which the modal path clears 20% a year over eighteen months (29.8 EUR at 16.0x; 30.2 EUR at the blended 16.2x; 27.4 EUR on the three-year test). Progress to Early-Stage rather than park. Conviction: medium on the business and the demand; a working hypothesis on the return, because the return leg rests on the interest line and the sector's multiple, neither of which the company controls. The park rule does not bite: no D or F on management ('No mediocre management' B), business quality ('Business' B), predictability ('Transmission' B) or trackability ('Leading indicators' C). Triggers named: a book-to-bill below 1.0x at the 9 November 2026 trading update or at FY2026, or the 902 EURm of options not exercised through the Q4 2026 season; a reported half-year adjusted EBIT margin below 26% (Invalidate); gross margin below 33% (Alarm); net debt to EBITDA above 2.5x at late 2027 with no asset sale under way (Invalidate), or at or above 3.5x, the covenant (Invalidate); a new acquisition before HGH is integrated (Alarm); tube lead times above 20 months, Harder below 15,000 tubes, net working capital above 43% of revenue, Kappa below 35 EURm in FY2026 (Alarms).
case: - The thesis: Theon is a contracted demand-inflection case in European soldier optronics, compelling at the operating line and only adequate at the shareholder's line at 30.96 EUR. The company has turned a policy-backed rearmament cycle into a 1.46 EURbn backlog and a 26.2% margin, but financed its expansion with 8.6m new shares and about 550 EURm of peak net debt, so EBITDA growing at about 30% a year reaches EPS at about 20%, and the modal return is about 17% a year over eighteen months and 15% over three years against the 20% bar. At about 30 EUR, 3% below the price, the modal path clears the bar.

- The external force is sector-wide, structural and contracted. European order intake across Morgan Stanley's coverage +25% to over 85 EURbn, aggregate backlog a record 438 EURbn (September 2026); NATO 5% of GDP by 2035 with 3.5% core; Germany 180 EURbn by 2030; SAFE 150 EURbn; militaries moving to one-to-one soldier equipping. Theon's 1 EURbn OCCAR framework (100,000 devices for Germany, 4,000 for Belgium, December 2025) is the largest night-vision procurement in NATO history. Direction by force: demand tailwind intensifying; core competition mild tailwind (the US primes ITAR-blocked, the European primes avoid Theon's markets), headwind at the platform and upstream edges; regulation tailwind (Buy-European 35% non-EU component cap, EU design authority, Omnibus V ten-year frameworks); own cycle turning up (experts' peak 2028 to 2029); macro neutral except the cost of money; supply side headwind D; the sector multiple a headwind to the price (C).

- The internal change is broad and leverage-funded: guidance raised twice in 2026 (A); balance-sheet utilisation B with the 'dangerous leverage' flag partly present (0.4x to 0.5x of covenant headroom); strategy pivot to 50/50 by 2029 resourced (B, empire-building flag plausible, five transactions in twelve months); acquisitions coherent and delivering (Kappa 11 points of H1 growth, a 42 EURm order) but discipline unproven at HGH's price (B); new products A (PHYLAX over 40 EURm, Kappa 42 EURm plus 27 EURm options, 100 EURm thermal clip-on, 70 EURm IdZ, record 25 EURm Harder third-party order); new geographies B (Europe still 83.1% of backlog); standards B; shareholder returns D (payout cut to 20% to 30%, rights issue at 30% discount); the Exosens reversal C; price rises C (industry prices up 2.5x to 3.0x since 2022 but passed through back-to-back, OCCAR "priced competitively"); no chief-executive change (D, an absence); perimeter widening (F, an absence).
counter_case: - At the whole-case level: Theon is a cyclical peak bought with leverage. European soldier-equipment demand is a two-to-three-year replenishment surge that peaks in 2027 to 2029, as the company's own former managers say; the largest contract is an agency framework priced for volume, and agency buying rises to 40% of European procurement by 2030, so the 26% margin is a pre-OCCAR artefact that compresses to the 15% to 18% the experts expect as volumes roll off; the founder has spent the peak's cash and about 550 EURm of debt on a supplier's minority stake with no control, a French acquisition at 18.5x EBITDA and a scatter of platform and AI ventures where Theon has no proven edge; free cash flow on FactSet's definition was 16.9% of net income in FY2025 and working capital eats 41 cents of every revenue euro; the balance sheet reaches 3.0x to 3.1x against a 3.5x covenant in the very quarter a ceasefire could delay the tranches; and the precedent for the fix is a rights issue at a 30% discount. On that reading the stock de-rates from 16.4x on peak earnings to the crash band of 10.1x on falling ones, 19.1 EUR or lower, and Deutsche Bank's free-cash-flow-yield value of 18.00 EUR is the honest number. The sector has already de-rated 20% to 38% over twelve months.

- Conceded: the timing of the leverage is poor and self-inflicted; the free-cash-flow record on any definition but the company's is weak; the Exosens stake is a governance oddity we would not have made; the R&D budget (2.8% of revenue) does not support the software ambition; the drop-through sensitivity shows the modal return falling to a D on a modest adverse ratio.
triggers: - Backlog conversion: a book-to-bill below 1.0x at the 9 November 2026 update or at FY2026, or the 902 EURm of options not exercised through the Q4 2026 season, would change the view; the record puts conversion at about 75%.

- Margin: a reported half-year adjusted EBIT margin below 26% invalidates; gross margin below 33% is the alarm; the record puts the margin holding at about 70%; the experts' 15% to 18% at the cycle's peak is the skew.

- Deleveraging: net debt to EBITDA above 2.5x at late 2027 (the H1 2027 report in September 2027 is the named check) with no asset sale under way invalidates; at or above 3.5x, the covenant, invalidates at any time; a new acquisition before HGH is integrated is the alarm; the record puts deleveraging at about 65%.

- The multiple: no sector de-rating inside eighteen months is put at 55%, so a de-rating is plausible; the re-rating needs both a cleaner balance sheet and a sector that stops falling, and neither is given better than two-to-one.
- Tube supply: lead times above 20 months or Harder below 15,000 tubes are the alarms; the record puts supply holding to 2030 at about 80%.
- Other alarms: net working capital above 43% of revenue; Kappa revenue below 35 EURm in FY2026.

items.criterion: Industry RS below 30, read each Friday

bullets.text: Sell signal at every Friday reading since 4-Sep; Defence's Industry RS was 13 on Fri 30-Oct, 17 points below its line.
Defence's Industry RS has read 13 seven times running, although Defence rose 9.5% from 8 to 30-Oct.
While it lasts, the rules sell the whole Theon holding when its replacement is bought, under your one-off in/out link.

items.criterion: The 200D MA of relative price flat or falling over the month, read each Friday

bullets.text: Sell signal: Theon's relative 200D MA fell 1.17% over the month to 30-Oct, from (0.92%) a week earlier.
Turning it up needs relative price 59% higher by Fri 6-Nov, or about 7% higher held through November.
The sell signal will very probably stand at the 6-Nov and 13-Nov Friday readings.

items.criterion: Sector RS below 50 with Stock RS below 70, read at the month-end

bullets.text: Sell signal at the 30-Oct month-end: Theon's Sector RS was 21 and Stock RS 32.
Since the 23-Oct Friday Theon's Sector RS rose from 8 to 21 and Stock RS from 22 to 32.
Ending it at the 30-Nov month-end needs Sector RS of 50 or Stock RS of 70, still 29 and 38 points away.

items.criterion: SS Sales or SS PT Net Upgrade Breadth below zero AND Stock RS below 50, read at the month-end

bullets.text: Sell signal at the 30-Oct month-end: Theon's SS PT Net Upgrade Breadth was (25%), none raising and two cutting of 8, with Stock RS 32.
The Framework 14 Reader computed this test in the 2-Nov 14:31 rebuild; Theon's SS Sales Net Upgrade Breadth is +25%, so the PT breadth alone gives the signal.

Ending it needs Stock RS of 50 or two PT raises with no new cut; ING's 15-Sep PT cut drops out of FactSet's 100-day count around 24-Dec if the window is in calendar days, or in early February 2027 if in trading days (the sources read do not say which).

items.criterion: Relative price more than 25% below its 52W high, read at the month-end

bullets.text: No sell signal: Theon's relative price was 20.8% below its 52W high at the 30-Oct month-end.
Theon was 25.5% below on the 28-Oct close and 26.9% below at the 30-Sep month-end.
At a flat market, a Theon close below €28.80 (5.3% lower) at the 30-Nov month-end gives this test a sell signal.

items.criterion: A tranche 30% below its highest close since purchase, with Stock RS below 70

bullets.text: No sell signal: both tranches' level is €26.82, 11.8% below the €30.42 close; Theon's Stock RS of 32 is below 70.
The distance widened from 6.9% on 23-Oct; Theon's 8-Oct low (€27.22) came within 1.5% of the level.
A Theon close below €26.82 triggers both tranches, each sold at the Tuesday session after its release, even under your link.

adds.criterion: The rules: no sell signal from the six Sell Criteria

bullets.text: Four of Theon's six Sell Criteria give sell signals on the Framework 14 readings of 30-Oct: Industry RS, the relative 200D MA, Sector RS with Stock RS, and SS PT Net Upgrade Breadth with Stock RS.
The rules allow no add while any Sell Criterion gives a sell signal.
Each signal would have to end: Industry RS and the relative 200D MA at a Friday, the others at a month-end.

adds.criterion: The rules: room below the holding's limit

bullets.text: Theon is 4.05% of capital against the 6.68% limit for a Middle Innings Core Investment, leaving 2.63%.
The limit governs purchases and never forces a sale; one 1.67% tranche would leave 0.96% of room.

adds.criterion: Where Theon stands for an add: pulling back or basing; may be retesting a rising MA or forming a volatility contraction pattern; healthily retesting a rising MA or breaking out of a volatility contraction pattern

bullets.text: None of the three: Theon's pullback has become a broken trend, with every MA from the 50D to the absolute 200D falling.
The Master Dashboard reads "Healthy Retest: Plausible (4 of 6 tests)" at the 50D MA, but that MA fell 8.15% in 20 sessions.
Higher lows holding above €27.92 would make it basing; a close above €31.98 on heavy volume would start a breakout.

adds.criterion: Your add trigger: a positive retest of a rising MA

bullets.text: Absent: Theon closed €0.02 below its 50D MA on 30-Oct, and that MA is falling, as are the 100D, 150D and absolute 200D.
Theon has bounced 11.8% from 8-Oct, but off no rising MA; its 20D MA has turned up only over the last five sessions (+0.74%) and is still down 7.18% over 20.
A Theon close above its absolute 200D MA (€31.54) with that MA rising again, then a pullback to it and a bounce.

adds.criterion: Your add trigger: a broadening of the case (momentum rising in guidance, sell-side estimates, technicals or peers)

bullets.text: Partly present: guidance is unchanged since its 7-Sep raise; FY2026 EPS and every year's EBITDA are rising, but FY2027 EPS is being cut.
Technicals improved (Stock RS 16 to 32 since 9-Oct), but Theon's peers rallied harder, so peer momentum is against Theon.
A book-to-bill of 1.0 or more on 9-Nov, then FY2027 EPS revisions and PT Net Upgrade Breadth turning up.
On 28-Oct you wrote in your Notion note: "Holding here looks like hope. This looks classic Stage 3 IMHO. Exit unless we can prove strong upgrade scope".
Item 1 (SP and MAs) finds four of your six trend-health tests failing, and item 4 (Consensus by named FY) finds FY2027 EPS cut, so the upgrade scope is not yet shown.
